subject: Bitcoin price drop
title: Why is bitcoin down? ETF outflows and $2 billion in forced selling
answer: Bitcoin fell to about $62,000 on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, its lowest level in about three months, before recovering to roughly $64,500. It is down about 15% in a week. Steady withdrawals from U.S. bitcoin ETFs, nearly $2 billion in forced liquidations of leveraged bets and hotter-than-expected inflation drove the slide.
in_the_news: The weekend drop hit while stock markets were closed, wiped out more than 300,000 leveraged traders and left bitcoin roughly half its record high of about $126,000, set in October 2025.
body:
The selling built through the week. Bitcoin slipped below $70,000 on Friday, Nov. 13, when more than $1 billion in leveraged positions were closed, then dropped again over the weekend. CoinGlass data showed about $1.96 billion in crypto liquidations over 24 hours, most of them traders betting on higher prices. When those bets lose enough, exchanges automatically sell, which pushes the price down further and can set off the next round.

Big investors have also been pulling money out. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.91 billion in net withdrawals over seven straight trading days from Nov. 5 to Nov. 13, according to Farside Investors, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for the largest share on Friday. October consumer prices rose 0.4%, a hotter reading that has traders weighing the chance of another Federal Reserve rate increase, which tends to hurt riskier assets. CoinDesk reported that analysts also pointed to money moving toward the heavily oversubscribed Anthropic IPO and to the turmoil around Nvidia's leadership change, while noting that the selloff was broad, with metals falling too.

Some traders on social media claimed the weekend plunge was manipulated, but no public evidence supports that, and many analysts blame excessive leverage instead. Analysts are watching whether bitcoin holds the $60,000 area; ETF flow data for the new week arrives after Monday's trading session.

faq.a: About $62,000 on Nov. 15, 2026, the lowest in roughly three months. It traded near $64,500 later that morning.
When a trader borrows to bet on a price move and the price goes the other way, the exchange closes the position automatically by selling. Many liquidations at once can deepen a drop.

faq.q: How far is bitcoin from its record?
faq.a: Around 49% below its all-time high of about $126,000, reached in October 2025.
No one knows. Analysts are watching support near $60,000, and ETF flows, which resume reporting after Monday's session, are a key signal. This is not financial advice.
